summary_hint: plan type + custodian, participant, statement period, and the total vs vested balance with the accessible (net-of-plan-loan, withdrawal-eligible) portion

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — validates source/independence of the statement

typed_core.name: plan_administrator_or_custodian
typed_core.why: identity — the custodian/administrator holding the plan assets

typed_core.name: plan_sponsor_or_employer
typed_core.why: identity/processor — the sponsoring employer; cross-checks employment and distinguishes employer plans

typed_core.name: participant_name
typed_core.why: identity — attach the plan to the borrower (AS-3/AS-4 count only borrower assets)

typed_core.name: plan_type
typed_core.why: AS-11/AS-3/AS-4 disambiguator — Traditional/Roth IRA vs 401(k)/403(b) changes access, penalty, and vesting rules

typed_core.name: account_number_masked
typed_core.prompt_hint: Never emit the full account number; mask to last 4

typed_core.name: statement_date
typed_core.why: identity/recency — as-of date of the balances

typed_core.name: statement_period_end
typed_core.why: AS-3/AS-4 use the most-recent balance; recency test key

typed_core.name: total_account_balance
typed_core.why: AS-11 (balance vs vested), AS-4 (reserve base before vesting/loan haircuts)

typed_core.name: vested_balance
typed_core.why: AS-11 (only the vested portion counts), AS-3, AS-4 — the true usable balance

typed_core.name: vested_percentage
typed_core.why: AS-11 disambiguator — used to compute the usable portion (the '60% vested' example)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture vested_percentage verbatim (e.g. '60%') alongside vested_balance so the engine can reconcile percent vs dollars

typed_core.name: plan_loan_balance
typed_core.why: AS-11 — loans outstanding reduce the accessible portion
typed_core.prompt_hint: A negative plan-loan line reduces the accessible portion; capture it as a positive balance in its own field

typed_core.name: plan_loan_payment
typed_core.why: processor — outstanding-loan monthly obligation; cheap future DTI/liability cross-check

typed_core.name: withdrawal_eligible_indicator
typed_core.why: AS-11 — whether terms permit access at all

typed_core.name: withdrawal_penalty_or_tax
typed_core.why: AS-11 — penalty/tax terms that affect usability

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity/classification — separates a periodic statement from a year-end/1099-R summary

typed_core.name: document_status_or_version
typed_core.why: processor — draft/final/corrected affects trust in the value

rejected.name: employee_contributions_ytd / employer_contributions_ytd
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL; no asset rule consumer (contribution flow, not usable balance)

rejected.name: required_minimum_distribution
rejected.reason: no consumer; RMD is a retiree concern, not reserves

rejected.name: plan_loan_payoff_terms
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL; AS-11 needs balance + restrictions, not the amortization schedule

rejected.name: investment_allocation
rejected.reason: no rule reads per-fund allocation; aggregate balances suffice

rejected.name: party_addresses / property_address / loan_number
rejected.reason: not on a plan statement / no consumer

rejected.name: signature_blocks / notary_block
rejected.reason: a plan statement is not executed

encoding_variations: Vested amount stated as a dollar vested_balance, a vested_percentage, or both — capture both; a percent alone requires the total to compute the usable dollars (the AS-11 example)
Plan loan appears as 'Outstanding Loan Balance', 'Loan(s) Payable', or a negative line in the balance roll-up — a negative is a liability, not a balance
Plan type stated as words ('Traditional IRA', 'Roth 401(k)'), a plan section code, or only in a fine-print disclosure — Roth vs Traditional changes withdrawal tax/penalty
Availability stated as 'Available to Withdraw', 'Loan Available', or 'Distributable Amount' — all map to available_for_withdrawal_or_loan; keep the label context

open_questions.q: No nested list — AS rules use aggregate vested/available balances
options: add investment_allocation (flat-row) if a rule discounts reserves by fund/asset class
open_questions.recommendation: none — confirm with Priya that no rule discounts reserves by fund/asset class; if one lands, investment_allocation (flat-row) becomes the one list

open_questions.q: vested_percentage degraded to str — no percent coercer exists
options: dollar vested_balance is the sole rule input
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the engine parses '60%' to 0.60 downstream for the AS-11 usable-portion compute, or whether the dollar vested_balance should be the sole rule input

open_questions.q: withdrawal_eligible_indicator bool to str — no boolean coercer
open_questions.recommendation: stored as verbatim str; confirm AS-11 reads it as a string flag

open_questions.q: plan_loan_payment inclusion — weak consumer (no DTI rule in this packet)
open_questions.recommendation: keep — cheap and a likely liability cross-check

open_questions.q: statement_date vs statement_period_end — may coincide on some plan statements

notes: This is a RETIREMENT asset: the decision-relevant figure is the accessible amount — vested, net of any plan loan, and withdrawal/loan-eligible — not the gross balance.
Report penalty/eligibility language verbatim; do not judge usability — rules judge, the extractor describes.
statement_period_start reason_class was set to processor as a best guess: its 'recency/coverage' why cites no rule id and names no explicit reason_class.
